/-!
# Conjecture 4.11

by G. Baumslag

Let $F$ be the free group of rank 2 in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not
finitely presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a set $W$ of laws. A law
is a word $w$ in the free group $F_\infty$ on the countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \ldots$, and a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every
substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. Every variety is defined by some
set of laws $W$. The free group of rank $2$ in the variety defined by $W$ is the
relatively free group $F_2 / W(F_2)$, where $F_2$ is the (absolutely) free group of
rank $2$ and $W(F_2)$ is its verbal subgroup, the subgroup generated by all values of
the words $w \in W$ on $F_2$.

The multiplicator of $F$ is its Schur multiplicator, the second integral homology
group $M(F) = H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$. By Hopf's formula this is $(R \cap [G, G]) / [R, G]$
for any presentation $F = G / R$ with $G$ free.

"Finitely presented" refers to $F$ as an abstract group (finitely many generators and
finitely many relators), not to presentations relative to the variety. "Infinitely
generated" means not finitely generated as an abelian group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

lemma conj_lift {G : Type*} [Group G] (f : ℕ → G) (c : G) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) :

instance verbalSubgroup_normal (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal := by
  refine ⟨fun n hn c => ?_⟩
  refine Subgroup.closure_induction (fun x hx => ?_) ?_ (fun x y _ _ ihx ihy => ?_)
    (fun x _ ihx => ?_) hn
  · obtain ⟨w, hw, f, rfl⟩ := hx
    exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, fun i => c * f i * c⁻¹, (conj_lift f c w).symm⟩
  · simp
  · rw [← conj_mul]
    exact mul_mem ihx ihy
  · rw [← conj_inv]
    exact inv_mem ihx
blocks.docstring:

`W(G)` is normal.

abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  FreeGroup (Fin n) ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n))
blocks.docstring:
The free group of rank `n` in the variety of groups defined by the set of laws `W`, i.e.
the relatively free group `Fₙ / W(Fₙ)`, the quotient of the (absolutely) free group `Fₙ` of
rank `n` by its verbal subgroup.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup, PresentedGroup (PresentedGroup would need the verbal subgroup as relators anyway); no relatively free groups in Mathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.11».RelativelyFreeGroup
justification.why_needed: Abbreviation for the free group of rank n in the variety defined by W, i.e. `FreeGroup (Fin n) ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n))`, the standard construction of relatively free groups.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma satisfiesLaw_relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (n : ℕ) {w : FreeGroup ℕ}
    (hw : w ∈ W) : SatisfiesLaw (RelativelyFreeGroup W n) w := by
  intro f
  choose f' hf' using fun i => QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (f i)
  have : FreeGroup.lift f =
      (QuotientGroup.mk' (verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n)))).comp (FreeGroup.lift f') := by
    ext i
    simp [hf']
  rw [this, MonoidHom.comp_apply, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, f', rfl⟩
blocks.docstring:
The free group of rank `n` in the variety defined by `W` satisfies every law in `W`, i.e.
it belongs to the variety.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) := Group.fg_iff.2
    ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

lemma isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) := by
  refine ⟨n, ∅, Set.finite_empty, ⟨?_⟩⟩

noncomputable abbrev schurMultiplicator (G : Type) [Group G] : ModuleCat ℤ :=
  groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ)
blocks.docstring:
The Schur multiplicator `M(G) = H₂(G, ℤ)` of a group `G`: its second homology group with
trivial integral coefficients.

justification.closest_existing_considered: groupHomology.H2 / groupHomology (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) 2 (this is exactly what the abbrev unfolds to); Hopf-formula quotient (R ⊓ commutator G)/[R,G] was considered but the homological definition is canonical and avoids further bespoke definitions.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.11».schurMultiplicator
justification.why_needed: Readable abbreviation for the Schur multiplicator M(G) = H₂(G, ℤ) as `groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ)`; Mathlib has group homology but no named Schur multiplier.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over all varieties of groups: for every variety 𝔙, if the relatively free (i.e. free in 𝔙) group F of rank 2 is not finitely presented as an abstract group, then its Schur multiplicator H₂(F, ℤ) (equivalently (R ∩ [G,G])/[R,G] for any presentation F = G/R with G free) is not finitely generated as an abelian group; note 'finitely presented' means as an abstract group, not relative to the variety, and 'infinitely generated' means not finitely generated.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are faithful in substance (variety = set of laws W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ or HSP-closed class; F = F₂/W(F₂) or an abstract group with the relative universal property; 'finitely presented' as an abstract group via PresentedGroup with finitely many generators/relators; multiplicator = Mathlib's H₂(F,ℤ) with trivial coefficients, or Hopf's formula in c02; 'infinitely generated' = ¬ finitely generated abelian group; answer(True) = positive answer). c08 was chosen as the clearest and best-tested: explicit `SatisfiesLaw`, textbook verbal subgroup (`Subgroup.closure` of word values) with a proved `Normal` instance, an API lemma showing F₂/W(F₂) satisfies every law of W (so it lies in the variety), `IsFinitelyPresented → Group.FG`, and a named `schurMultiplicator` abbrev. Edits: renamed `FinitelyPresented` → `IsFinitelyPresented` (Mathlib predicate naming, as in most other candidates), added c04's test that the rank-n free group of the variety of all groups (W = ∅) is finitely presented, minor docstring tightening. Compiles with only the `sorry` warning, also under the repository's CI linter options.

namespace Kourovka.«4.11»

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w`, a word in the free group on the countably many variables
`x₀, x₁, …`, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the
variables. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The verbal subgroup `W(G)` of a group `G` determined by a set `W` of laws: the subgroup
generated by all values `w(g₀, g₁, …)` of the words `w ∈ W` on `G`. -/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}

/-- Conjugating the value of a word gives the value of the word at the conjugated
substitution. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma conj_lift {G : Type*} [Group G] (f : ℕ → G) (c : G) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) :
    c * FreeGroup.lift f w * c⁻¹ = FreeGroup.lift (fun i => c * f i * c⁻¹) w :=
  FreeGroup.lift_unique ((MulAut.conj c).toMonoidHom.comp (FreeGroup.lift f)) (fun x => by simp)

/-- The set of values of the words in `W` is closed under conjugation, so the verbal subgroup
`W(G)` is normal. -/
instance verbalSubgroup_normal (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal := by
  refine ⟨fun n hn c => ?_⟩
  refine Subgroup.closure_induction (fun x hx => ?_) ?_ (fun x y _ _ ihx ihy => ?_)
    (fun x _ ihx => ?_) hn
  · obtain ⟨w, hw, f, rfl⟩ := hx
    exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, fun i => c * f i * c⁻¹, (conj_lift f c w).symm⟩
  · simp
  · rw [← conj_mul]
    exact mul_mem ihx ihy
  · rw [← conj_inv]
    exact inv_mem ihx

/-- The verbal subgroup for the empty set of laws (the variety of all groups) is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma verbalSubgroup_empty (G : Type*) [Group G] : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- The free group of rank `n` in the variety of groups defined by the set of laws `W`, i.e.
the relatively free group `Fₙ / W(Fₙ)`, the quotient of the (absolutely) free group `Fₙ` of
rank `n` by its verbal subgroup. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  FreeGroup (Fin n) ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n))

/-- The free group of rank `n` in the variety defined by `W` satisfies every law in `W`, i.e.
it belongs to the variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma satisfiesLaw_relativelyFreeGroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (n : ℕ) {w : FreeGroup ℕ}
    (hw : w ∈ W) : SatisfiesLaw (RelativelyFreeGroup W n) w := by
  intro f
  choose f' hf' using fun i => QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (f i)
  have : FreeGroup.lift f =
      (QuotientGroup.mk' (verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup (Fin n)))).comp (FreeGroup.lift f') := by
    ext i
    simp [hf']
  rw [this, MonoidHom.comp_apply, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, f', rfl⟩

/-- A group `G` is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) := Group.fg_iff.2
    ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/-- A free group of finite rank is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) := by
  refine ⟨n, ∅, Set.finite_empty, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  have h : Subgroup.normalClosure (∅ : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) = ⊥ :=
    le_bot_iff.1 (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _))
  exact ((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq h).trans QuotientGroup.quotientBot).symm

/-- The free group of rank `n` in the variety of all groups is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma isFinitelyPresented_relativelyFreeGroup_empty (n : ℕ) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup ∅ n) := by
  obtain ⟨m, rels, h, ⟨e⟩⟩ := isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup n
  exact ⟨m, rels, h, ⟨((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq (verbalSubgroup_empty _)).trans
    QuotientGroup.quotientBot).trans e⟩⟩

/-- The Schur multiplicator `M(G) = H₂(G, ℤ)` of a group `G`: its second homology group with
trivial integral coefficients. -/
noncomputable abbrev schurMultiplicator (G : Type) [Group G] : ModuleCat ℤ :=
  groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ)

/--
Let $F$ be the free group of rank 2 in some variety of groups. If $F$ is not
finitely presented, is the multiplicator of $F$ necessarily infinitely generated?

Here the variety is the one defined by an arbitrary set $W$ of laws, $F = F_2 / W(F_2)$
is its free group of rank $2$, "finitely presented" refers to $F$ as an abstract group,
and the multiplicator of $F$ is the Schur multiplicator $H_2(F, \mathbb{Z})$, which is
"infinitely generated" if it is not finitely generated as an abelian group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.11» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      ¬ IsFinitelyPresented (RelativelyFreeGroup W 2) →
        ¬ AddGroup.FG (schurMultiplicator (RelativelyFreeGroup W 2)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.11»

items: Varieties of groups are modelled by arbitrary sets of laws W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ) (words in countably many variables x₀, x₁, …); by definition (and Birkhoff's theorem for the HSP formulation) every variety is defined by some such W, so ∀ W ranges over all varieties. Different W may define the same variety, which is harmless for a universal statement.

The free group of rank 2 in the variety defined by W is taken to be F₂/W(F₂) (quotient of FreeGroup (Fin 2) by the verbal subgroup), the standard construction of relatively free groups; the verbal subgroup is defined as Subgroup.closure of the set of word values, with normality proved.

'Finitely presented' is formalized as an abstract-group property: isomorphic to PresentedGroup rels for a finite type Fin n of generators and a finite set of relators (the notebook's intended meaning per the decomposition notes, not finite presentability within the variety).

The multiplicator is the Schur multiplicator H₂(F, ℤ), taken directly from Mathlib's `groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ F ℤ)` (inhomogeneous chains, trivial integral coefficients), rather than via Hopf's formula; the docstring records Hopf's formula for orientation only.
'Infinitely generated' is formalized as `¬ AddGroup.FG` of the carrier of the ModuleCat ℤ object; this is equivalent to `¬ Module.Finite ℤ` (checked via Module.Finite.iff_addGroup_fg).

Positive answer: answer(True) ⇔ for every variety, non-finitely-presented relatively free group of rank 2 has non-finitely-generated multiplicator. Degenerate varieties (trivial variety, variety of all groups, finite relatively free groups) give finitely presented F and are excluded by the hypothesis, matching the source.
Universe: F lives in Type (as required by `Rep ℤ F` with ℤ : Type); this is no restriction since F₂/W(F₂) is a Type-level object.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities resolved per the decomposition notes: (1) 'some variety' is read as an implicit universal quantifier over all varieties, encoded as ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ) (every variety is defined by a set of laws in countably many variables; distinct W defining the same variety is harmless under ∀). (2) 'finitely presented' is as an abstract group, not relative to the variety. (3) 'multiplicator' = Schur multiplicator H₂(F, ℤ) (`groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ F ℤ)`), which equals Hopf's (R ∩ [G,G])/[R,G]; c02 used the Hopf-formula quotient directly, which is also correct but more baroque, so the homology form was preferred. (4) 'infinitely generated' = ¬ AddGroup.FG (equivalently ¬ Module.Finite ℤ). Universe: F must live in Type because Mathlib's `Rep ℤ F` requires k and G in the same universe; the concrete quotient F₂/W(F₂) is in Type, so this is no restriction. Boundary cases: W = ∅ gives F₂ (finitely presented, hypothesis fails), W ∋ x₀ gives the trivial group (finitely presented); both are vacuous exactly as in the source. c01 (HSP-structure) and c05 (abstract universal property) are also faithful alternatives but the concrete construction is more transparent.
